text:
anna-support: escalating from ACME (private VPC). Customer sees intermittent 401s and 429s during a morning traffic spike. P99 latency jumped from 180ms -> 1.6s. They run a customer-managed gateway (Envoy) in k8s and say ingress annotations were recently changed. They provided logs and a repro.

anna-support: reproduction they ran (copied from customer):
```
# simple burst from their gateway node
for i in {1..300}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redwood-key>' http://gateway.acme.internal/v1/completions &
done; wait
```
Response mix: a lot of 200s, bursts of 429, occasional 401. No consistent pattern by path.

matt-eng-sre: thanks — can you paste the gateway ingress/nginx/envoy annotations (the customer-side config)? 429s + 401s together sounds like either auth token exhaustion or a proxy returning cached 401s while rate limiter trips.

anna-support: pasted config from customer (redacted):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: redwood-gateway
  annotations:
    envoyproxy.io/ratelimit: "true"
    envoyproxy.io/ratelimit-descriptors: "route,client"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "100"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rpm: "600"
spec: ...
```
They also have an external rate-limit-service behind the gateway returning headers `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`.

jia-eng-runtime: a few quick checks:
- verify the gateway is not reusing old upstream auth tokens when rate-limited (some proxies cache a 401 response for `cache-control: no-cache` misconfigs)
- confirm token refresh concurrency (Auth service might be hitting its own rate cap when multiple upstreams refresh simultaneously)
- check the gateway logs for ratelimit action type (local vs remote). Envoy will log `http_conn_manager.ratelimit`/`envoy.ratelimit` entries.

matt-eng-sre: also try to reproduce locally from our side: port-forward the gateway service and run `hey` to simulate concurrency:
```bash
kubectl port-forward svc/redwood-gateway 8080:80 -n redwood
# from jump box
hey -n 2000 -c 200 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <test-key>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' http://localhost:8080/v1/completions
```
That will reveal whether the gateway rate limiter triggers on source IP or client header, and whether burst smoothing exists.

sasha-cs: ACME says their traffic is very spiky (batch jobs at 08:30 that fan out) and they increased `limit-connections` last week. They want a quick remediation — ideally avoid 401s (auth) and reduce 429s during the spike.

jia-eng-runtime: remediation checklist (quick):
- increase `burst` / token bucket `capacity` on the gateway for that route (allow short bursts)
- enable splay/jitter on the ingress rate limiter so many clients don't refresh simultaneously
- ensure auth token refreshes are rate-limited per-instance (use a background single-flight token fetch)
- short-term: apply a route-level `retry_on`/`num_retries` with `per_try_timeout` so transient 429s get retried (but be careful with downstream load)
- long-term: recommend client-side exponential backoff + jitter, and consider moving ACME to dedicated capacity if steady high throughput

matt-eng-sre: examples of envoy token-bucket patch we suggested to other customers:
```yaml
rate_limit:
  descriptors:
  - key: route
    value: /v1/completions
    rate_limit:
      unit: minute
      requests_per_unit: 1000
      burst: 250
```
Tune `burst` to absorb the short fanout; `requests_per_unit` controls steady-state.

anna-support: customer also reported weird billing spikes correlated with the morning. Could be retries from clients or our SDK retrying on 429s. ACME uses an internal retrier that retries on any non-200.

jia-eng-runtime: ask them to capture a sampling of request-id headers for the spike window and provide both gateway logs and our request-id from the upstream. Check for duplicate requests (same request-id) or many retries within <1s. If it's our SDK retries, we should disable aggressive retries in their SDK config.

matt-eng-sre: quick mitigation we can push to them immediately:
1) add a conservative `burst` bump in gateway descriptor for the route.
2) add `x-envoy-decorator-operation` and `x-envoy-internal` to mark internal retries.
3) set auth-service rate limit exemption for token refresh endpoints so auth doesn't get blocked during fanout.

anna-support: I asked ACME to run the `hey` test from their control plane and share the exact command + capture. They did and attached a short PCAP and gateway logs. Logs show repeated `HTTP/1.1 429` with header `x-ratelimit-reason: local_bucket_exhausted` and an intermittent `401` that happens right after a 429 for a subset of requests.

jia-eng-runtime: that pattern suggests the gateway returns 429 then the upstream client begins refresh flow that results in auth failures (race when token is expired). Sequence: many 429s -> client retries or refresh -> auth service is overloaded -> some refreshes fail -> 401s ripple back.

sasha-cs: ACME asked if we can provide a small playbook to hand to their infra team. They want commands and a minimal patch.

anna-support: provided playbook (minimal):
```text
1) Patch ingress descriptor: bump burst to 300 for /v1/completions route and set refill to 1000/minute.
2) Enable splay on token refresh: set singleflight=true in auth client and add jitter 100-500ms to refresh.
3) Add a short client-side retry policy (max 2 retries, backoff with jitter) in their SDK.
4) Monitor: watch for x-ratelimit-remaining and request-id duplication for 2 hours after deploy.
```

matt-eng-sre: I'll take ownership of the triage. I'll work with ACME's infra in the next 60 minutes and roll the patch. @jia-eng-runtime if we see auth service saturation we'll throttle token refresh calls centrally.

deploy-bot: deploy started for patch redwood/patches#452 -> ingress descriptor bump (deploy id d-7732).

anna-support: customer confirmed they'll hold off on client sweeping changes until we deploy the patch and observe behaviour. I'll update the ticket after the 30 min post-deploy check.

matt-eng-sre: follow-ups: capture kernel socket stats on gateway node during next spike (`ss -s`, `netstat -s`), check envoy runtime counters `server.ratelimit.descriptor_entries` and `http.ingress_ratelimited` and send to us if anomalies persist.

jia-eng-runtime: note for records: this is a classic cascade (burst -> rate limiter -> auth refresh -> auth capacity hit -> 401s). Remediation path: absorb burst + smooth refresh + client backoff.

anna-support: thanks team — updating ticket and tagging support escalation owner.
